verses.text: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our home through all generations.
Before the mountains were born, before you made the earth and the world, you are God, from forever in the past to forever in the future.
You turn people back to dust. You say, "Go back to dust, you humans."
To you, a thousand years are like yesterday that has just gone by, like a few hours in the night.
You sweep people away like a dream. They are like new grass in the morning.
In the morning it springs up and grows, but by evening it dries up and dies.
We are destroyed by your anger. We are terrified by your fury.
You have put our sins in front of you, our secret sins in the light of your presence.
All our days pass away under your anger. Our years end with a sigh.
We live for seventy years, or eighty if we are strong. But even our best years are full of hard work and sorrow. They quickly pass, and we fly away.
Who understands the power of your anger? Your fury is as great as the fear you deserve.
Teach us to count our days carefully, so that we may have wise hearts.
Turn back to us, LORD! How long will it be? Have pity on your servants!
Satisfy us every morning with your faithful love, so we can sing for joy and be glad all our lives.
Make us glad for as many days as you have made us suffer, for as many years as we have seen trouble.
Let your servants see what you do. Let their children see your glory.
May the kindness of the Lord our God be on us. Make the work of our hands succeed. Yes, make the work of our hands succeed.
